title: SQL Injection in auth_handler.py:get_user()
description: User-controlled input 'username' is concatenated directly into a SQL query at line 28. An attacker can manipulate the query to bypass authentication or exfiltrate data. Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=?", (username,))

files_content.samples/sonar/auth_handler.py:
import sqlite3

DB_PATH = "app.db"
ADMIN_PASSWORD = "hardcoded_secret_123"  # noqa: S105 — hardcoded credential (SONAR S2068)


def get_db():
    return sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)


def get_user(username: str) -> dict | None:
    """Fetch a user record by username.

    WARNING: This function is intentionally vulnerable to SQL injection.
    The 'username' parameter is concatenated directly into the query string
    instead of using a parameterised query, violating OWASP A03:2021.
    """
    conn = get_db()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    # BAD: user-controlled input concatenated into SQL — CWE-89
    query = "SELECT id, username, email, role FROM users WHERE username = '" + username + "'"
    cursor.execute(query)  # line 28 — flagged by SonarQube python:S3649
    row = cursor.fetchone()
    conn.close()
    if row is None:
        return None
    return {"id": row[0], "username": row[1], "email": row[2], "role": row[3]}


def authenticate(username: str, password: str) -> bool:
    user = get_user(username)
    if user is None:
        return False
    # Simplified — real code would hash+compare
    return password == ADMIN_PASSWORD

metadata.rule_name: Database queries should not be vulnerable to injection attacks
